newsitem.title: ITALY: No luck for Italian lottery law suit.
newsitem.headline: No luck for Italian lottery law suit.

text.p: Efforts to scrap the results of Italy's presitigious New Year lottery and hold a new draw were rejected by a regional court on Wednesday.
The lottery was thrown into a spin last week when a technical hitch snarled the draw for the fifth prize, worth two billion lire ($1.2 million).

A winning number was extracted, but officials failed to notice that some of the balls had not fallen into one of the seven draw machines. Television replays clearly showed the block and the next day the jury gave the prize to someone else.
The foul-up scandalised lottery-loving Italians and a consumer protection group, Codacons, asked the court to nulify the whole draw and order a re-run.

However the Lazio administrative court ruled that there were no grounds to invalidate the lottery. Codacons chairman, Carlo Rienzi, told reporters immediately after the decision that he would appeal against the ruling.
The identity of the original winner, dubbed in Italian newspapers "Mr Happy Forawhile", has remained a mystery. The ticket was sold in a small eastern Italian town.
